text: Hello, boys and girls, glad to see you.Last period, we talked about different types of pronouns, and the problems we might have when we use them, especially in writing.Today, we will continue to talk about grammar.Many of my students often come to me and ask, Ms.Chen, how can I make my writing more logical and interesting?Well, today's lesson will help you a lot.Do you remember our main character, John?What kind of person is he?Yes, a very sensible man.What shows that he was sensible?What did he do?Toning1.He asked to see the manager when the clerk refused to allow Charlie into the hotel again.After he checked in, he asked about the location of the fire exit.Before firemen came, he did many right things to keep himself safe from danger.Thank you.Have a look at these sentences.They all have something in common.The words in red are clauses used to provide more details.What is an adverbial clause?First, let's think about what an adverb is.An adverb describes a verb and says when, why, how, where, etc.Read this sentence.John's troubles began then.Here, then is an adverb.It is used to tell when the troubles began.The answer is then.And read this one.John's troubles began as soon as he walked into the Dragon Hotel.Still, when did the troubles begin?As soon as he walked into the Dragon Hotel.Here, John's troubles began is the main clause.The underlined part is a clause used to describe the verb began in the main clause and say when.It functions just like an adverb.We call it an adverbial clause.And the phrase as soon as connects the two clauses together.We call it a subordinating conjunction.The adverbial clause is a kind of subordinate clause.Sub means under.It's under the main clause, which means the main clause is a more important one.An adverbial clause can come either after the main clause or before it.Take this sentence as an example.We can also say, as soon as John walked into the Dragon Hotel, his troubles began.Just notice, when we begin a sentence with an adverbial clause, we should put a comma at the end of the clause before the main clause.There are many types of adverbial clauses.Today, we will mainly focus on three of them.Adverbial clause of time, reason, and concession.We can also call the third one adverbial clause of contrast.Read the following sentences.What do the clauses in green tell us?Yes, time.So we call them adverbial clauses of time.In such clauses, we use as soon as, before, after, when, while, as, since, until as subordinating conjunctions.Let's look at them in more detail.We arrested him as soon as he got out of the lift.It means, the moment he got out of the lift, we arrested him soon.As soon as refers to the moment or at the moment that something happens.只某事发生时即刻发生。We use before and after to talk about the order of events in the past or future.Before refers to some time that happens sooner than another point in time, while after is the opposite.Let's look at this sentence.Which event happened first?He checked in.The second event is that he asked about the location of the fire exit.In this case, we can also say he checked in before he asked about the location of the fire exit.But sometimes, we use before to say that the action or event in the before clause did not or may not happen.For example, before we could move, Gorg pressed a button on the wall beside him.Had we ever moved?Actually, Gorg's pressing a button prevented us from moving.Now, read this sentence.He will probably go to university after he leaves school.The action of leaving school will happen first.Pay attention.When we talk about the things in the future, we should use the present tense in the subordinate clause.We don't say after he will leave school.What about as, when and while?They mean at or during a time that 当什么的时候。We can use them to connect two events happening at the same time.These are the sentences we learned before.We can use other simple or continuous verb forms in the clauses.The continuous form emphasizes an action that interrupts or occurs during the progress of another action.从句用进行时,强调主句的动作是在从句动作过程中发生的。As, when and while can mean the same in some uses, but they can also have slightly different meanings.Compared to when and while, as sounds more formal and literary.In the following cases, we cannot use when as the conjunction.First, when a clause includes a verb with a meaning or a tense that expresses duration, 当从句中有一个表示延续的动词或时态时。Like this sentence, while she was on holiday.Be here is a verb that expresses duration.We use while to connect sentences, not when.Second, when we talk about two longer events or activities happening at the same time.当陈述两个同时进行的长动作时。For example, we were lying on the beach while they were playing volleyball.We have both verbs lie and play in the continuous tense.It shows that there are longer events or activities.In the following sentences, we cannot use while as the conjunction.First, when we have two single completed actions that happen at the same time or one happens right after another.当两个短动作同时发生或紧接着发生时。For example, I picked up the phone when it ran.Both verbs here are in the simple past, which shows they are completed actions.Second, when we introduce a single completed event that takes place in the middle of a longer activity or event.当在描述一个长动作进行过程中发生一个完结行为时。Weight would vary is a longer event, while here a big argument happens in the moment.We use the past continuous tense in the main clause and the simple past tense in the adverbial clause.We only use when to connect the two parts.Third, when we talk about the future.For example, when a new park opens, I would go there every day.What about until and since?Until means up to a time in the past or future.I waited there until you called me.Keep going until I tell you to stop.Pay attention, we use present verb forms to refer to the future after until.In this sentence, the children fled and did not stop until they were safe at home.Not until means not before a particular time or event.直到什么什么才。It means they stopped when they were safe at home, but not before then.In an adverbial clause of time, since means from the time in the past or until now.自从什么以来。We can use the past simple after since and the present perfect in the main clause.Since 引导的时间状语从句中,从句常使用一般过去,主句常使用现在完成时。Get bored?OK, let's have some practice.Complete the sentences with when, while, as soon as, after, before, since or until.It's task one on your worksheet.Now, check your answers.Have you got them right?Next, have a look at the second sentence.What does since mean here?Is this a clause of time?Of course not.Here, since introduces an adverbial clause of reason.原因状语从句。It shows why an action is done.It is generally introduced by because, as, since, etc.Because is common in both writing and speaking.When we use it, we focus on the reason.And the people we are speaking to don't have an idea or any previous knowledge of the situation.For example, I like my school because the teachers are very friendly.You won't know my reason until I tell you, right?I'm stressing that fact.As and since are more formal than because.We use since or as in the sense when the people we are speaking to know a little bit about the situation.We often use since or as when we want to focus more on the result than the reason.Let's look at the example.Since everybody is here or as everybody is here, let's begin our lesson.We are with different people, and they know that everybody is here.As he couldn't speak or since he couldn't speak, he had to make some gestures.The others knew the fact that he couldn't speak.The result was that he had to make some gestures.It wasn't surprising to see so.Now, look at these sentences.What do the words in green show?Right, contrast.Or in other words, difference.We call such clauses the adverbial clauses of concession.让不壮与从据 The contrast could be yes or no, positive or negative.正面的或负面的 It could be one idea and then a contrasting idea, or one expectation and one completely different result.Common conjunctions are although and though.They mean the same thing.Look at the first sentence.Owning only a few things usually makes people unhappy.This is the opposite of happy, a strong contrast.In the second sentence, many people thought it was Benjamin who invented electricity, but actually he didn't.The main clause is different from what one expects.Have a look at this sentence.Which word we use to complete it?Because or although?Gigi, what's your answer?I will use although.The sentence I like pizza a lot suggests the speaker might eat it every day.However, the word rarely tells he doesn't.There is a contrast between how he feels about pizza and how often he eats it.Good job.You are correct.Here, try these sentences.How will you complete them?Gigi, the first one, please.Although he is over 60, he can do 50 push-ups in a minute.Yes, usually old people are not strong enough to do a lot of sports, but he is opposite from our expectation.The second one, Tony.Although I failed in the test, my mom was not angry with me.Okay, you didn't do well in the test, and you thought your mom would be very angry, but the result was totally different.The clause shows the contrast.Thank you two for your examples.I believe the others can better understand the clause now with your help.When we use an adverbic clause of concession with although or though, we don't use but in the main sentence.The same goes for because and so.Now, open your textbook and turn to page 79.Match the two halves of the sentences in B2.Here are the answers.Next, you will practice adverbic clauses in your writing.Here is the situation.The fire at the Dragon Hotel has raised people's awareness of fire prevention.The community where Billy lives organized a family fire drill yesterday.Watch the video and take notes for what Billy's family did during the drill.It's task two on your worksheet.Okay, everyone.The test will begin shortly.When the fire alarm starts, you have three minutes to get out of the house.Ready?There's smoke.Get down.Don't be nervous, you two.Just do what we practiced.Got it?Yeah.Leave it to me.Go to the first exit.Hold on.Front door's on fire.No good.Option two.The window.Honey, the window's blocked too.It's all gonna be fine.We'll find a way out.Thirty seconds remaining.Mom, the back door.The third exit.That's right, the back door.Okay, come, hurry.Okay.Sarah.Ten seconds.I don't.Take care of our children.Don't be ridiculous.你真是神經病,我永遠不會讓你離開三、二、一恭喜你,你都成功了哇!太棒了,爹!時間到他們開始做什麼呢?他們跑出了房間他們做了什麼呢?他們一起下樓了但什麼都沒想到的事情發生了什麼事呢?爹掉下樓了他們從房子裡逃跑了嗎?從前面的門?不,他們用了後門那是什麼事呢?媽媽掉下樓了為什麼呢?她被滑倒了誰來幫忙呢?爹他把她帶走請檢查你的記錄既然你知道進一步的重要資訊請完成Billy's
